cohort: Deliveries in the United States between 2004 and 2014, categorized into women with PCOS (n = 14,882) and without PCOS (n = 9,081,906) using the Healthcare Cost and Utilization Project-Nationwide Inpatient Sample (HCUP-NIS) database
finding: Women with PCOS have an increased risk of experiencing PPROM, PTD, placental abruption, C/S delivery, chorioamnionitis, postpartum maternal infections, and congenital anomalies in their offspring.
mod_finding: Women with PCOS were more likely to deliver by cesarean section (C/S) compared to women without PCOS.
